title: Attribution lens: metric provenance and investigation checklist (WIP)
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a lightweight ‘attribution lens’ to help operators and owners quickly trace from an alerting symptom (dashboards/alerts) to the authoritative metric source, expected transformations, likely trace anchors, and a short investigation checklist. Aim: reduce time-to-blame and reduce noisy queries by standardizing provenance metadata and a compact operator playbook.

Scope
- Focused on inference/runtime metrics (latency, token counts, batching, KV cache hit/miss), routing fallbacks, and costy aggregation queries.
- Not covering user-facing product metrics or billing pipeline internals (except where they surface as per-token anomalies).
- Intentionally pragmatic: short decision trees, quick checks, links to deeper docs if needed.

Why we need this
- Multiple dashboards surface similar-sounding metrics from different pipelines (agent vs exporter vs app-level aggregation).
- Investigations often start with a chart, but the chart lacks clear provenance (is it raw gauge from exporter, derived from sampling, or post-processed in SQL?).
- Operators spend cycles re-running heavy queries during incidents. If provenance metadata and a checklist are paired with sampling-safe scratch queries, time to resolved incident should drop.

Metric provenance schema (proposal) – stored as dashboard widget annotation
- source_component: exporter | runtime-agent | aggregator | synthetic-probe
- collection_frequency: gauge | 1s | 10s | 1m | event-driven
- aggregation_window: none | p50/p95 p99-over 1m/5m/1h (string)
- derivation_sql_or_id: short id or SQL snippet (if applicable)
- owner: team or oncall alias
- expected_staleness_behavior: expected to drop to 0 on pod recycle? yes/no
- high_cost_tag: low | medium | high

Example annotation (for a latency p95 widget)
- source_component: runtime-agent
- collection_frequency: 10s
- aggregation_window: p95-1m
- derivation_sql_or_id: aggregator.v2/p95-window-1m
- owner: eng-serving-runtime-oncall
- expected_staleness_behavior: no
- high_cost_tag: low

Naming and labeling conventions (quick rules)
- metric names should include: service, surface, unit. e.g., inference.runtime.latency_ms.p95 or inference.kv_cache.hit_rate
- labels: tenant_id | model_version | route_name | deployment_zone
- avoid fragile labels for cardinality (no freeform user_email, prefer tenant_hash)
- dashboard widgets should include the provenance schema as a single-line annotation under the title.

Trace annotation anchors (how to link traces to metrics)
- Ensure every high-impact metric has a documented trace anchor: the span name and an example trace id format. E.g., inference.request span with tag request_id and model_version.
- If metric is derived from sampled traces (e.g., tail-latency from traces), include sample_rate and the SQL/transform used to upweight the sample.
- For KV cache metrics: annotate the span where KV lookup happens (span.name: kv.lookup) and include tags: cache_key_type, cache_hit_bool.

Sampling budget and back-of-envelope costs
- Default trace sampling for production: 1% for general traffic, 10% for egress-external calls and for requests > 1s latency.
- Keep a small high-fidelity bucket (0.1% of traffic) with full payload retention for deep postmortems; rotate retention to limit storage costs.
- Annotate dashboards with an estimated query cost for the widget (low/med/high) and a recommended cheap alternative (e.g., pre-aggregated counter, synthetic probe).

Dashboard composition notes (templates)
- Investigation-first mini-panel (3 rows):
  Row 1: Signal (p50/p95/p99) with provenance annotation + quick filter to tenant
  Row 2: Supporting health metrics (cpu/gpu utilization, queue-depth, batch-size distribution)
  Row 3: Trace links (last matching trace ids) + recent deploys and rollback flag
- For multi-tenant views: show median and 95th per-tenant sparklines (limit to top 15 by traffic) and provide a per-tenant drilldown link.

Investigation checklist (operator-friendly, sequence)
1) Confirm scope: Which widget/alert triggered? Copy provenance annotation.
2) Check owner: ping owner alias; check oncall rotation.
3) Fast sanity: any recent deploys (last 30m)? open PRs? (deploy-announce channel)
4) Correlate with infra: node restarts, GPU memory pressure, OOMs. Quick shell: kube events + recent node health metrics.
5) Query cheap proxies: if p95 spiked, check request queue size and batch-size hist; if queue grew, likely backpressure upstream.
6) Trace sample check: find a few traces around the spike using the annotated span name. If traces show repeated retries or blocking RPC, escalate to infra.
7) Check KV cache: if miss rate rose, fallback model variants may have fired; look at routing logs.
8) If metric derives from SQL, re-run the derivation locally but on truncated time window (1–5 minutes) to avoid heavy queries. Use the provided derivation id.
9) If noisy: mute alert for 10m and add 'noise' annotation to widget with reason. Document any follow-ups.

Cheap investigation queries (snippets to keep in a shared snippet library)
- recent-p95-fast: SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) as t, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) from fast_latency WHERE ts > now() - interval '15m' GROUP BY t ORDER BY t DESC LIMIT 15;
- kv-hit-sample: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE hit=true) / nullif(count(*),0) FROM kv_events WHERE ts > now() - interval '30m';
- trace-anchor-query (light): SELECT trace_id FROM spans WHERE span_name='inference.request' AND ts > now() - interval '30m' AND duration_ms > 1000 LIMIT 5;

Operational stories / short examples
- Story A: p95 spike that resolved after 4 minutes. Investigation found a single routing host that became CPU-throttled. The provenance annotation pointed to runtime-agent as source (10s scrape, p95-1m) so we pulled host metrics first and found an autoscaler lag.
- Story B: high token count with no latency change. Provenance showed derived token_count from aggregator.v2; trace anchors showed normal single-request paths but increased batch-size distribution; root cause — one client switched to an analytic mode that batch-sends long prompts. We added a per-tenant token guard.

Open questions / todo
- How do we automate embedding the provenance schema into dashboard widgets in Grafana? (investigate dashboard-as-code approach)
- Should we require a derivation id for any widget marked high_cost?
- Can we expose a one-click ‘re-run-light-query’ button (time-truncated) for heavy SQL widgets?

Appendix: quick links
- derived-metrics registry (confluence:DerivedMetrics-registry)
- trace-span-naming guidelines (confluence:Trace-Naming-Guide)
- alerting playbook (JIRA:OBS-144)

Notes to self
- next: sketch a small Grafana panel plugin that surfaces provenance on hover and shows estimated query cost.
- add a tiny onboarding checklist for new SREs: how to find derivation ids and run the cheap queries.

(End of WIP)
